intro.text: The homeland of the Shin in the far west of Roshar, where the highstorms are weak, the ground is covered in soil and grass, and stone is held sacred.

description.text: Farmers stand highest in Shin society. Farming villages and farmland are held holy, and outsiders may not enter them.

Warriors rank lowest of all, below craftsmen and even merchants, because they exist only to destroy. Anyone who picks up a weapon must take a stone and live out their life as a warrior, obeying whoever holds it in everything. The stone looks ordinary; the obedience is given freely.
Because stone is sacred to the Shin, they will not build with it; their homes are made of clay and earth.

Bargaining with the Shin runs backwards: each side plays down its own goods until they agree, and honesty is rewarded. Most merchants find this baffling, but the Thaylen Vstim is one of the few who understands it, and he does well. The Shin raise chickens, found nowhere else on Roshar, and sell them along with cloth, dried meat and the horses they are famous for.

The Shin follow Stone Shamanism. Stone is sacred, the soul passes into stone at death, and mountains have a spirit-soul of their own. Walking on stone or mining it is heresy, and those who do it are scorned as Stonewalkers. Metal is therefore precious, and Soulcast metal is preferred to mined. The Shin also refuse to trade for fabrials, apparently for reasons of faith.

Plants and animals in Shinovar need not survive highstorms and cannot live elsewhere. The ground is springy with soil and covered in grass that does not move, and the trees grow straight with their leaves left out. Fruits such as strawberries grow here, and the Shin raise chickens and horses, which also run wild.

Shinovar fills the far west of the continent between the Misted Mountains to the east and another range to the west, with several rivers running through it from the seas to the north and south. The mountains keep it from bordering any other nation.

Shin officials such as Farmers and Cooks do the actual farming and cooking as well as governing, unlike most rulers on Roshar. Some places also have a mayor. The Bondsmith Honorbearer, the only one chosen by civil rather than religious custom, is grand senator of all Shinovar.

The country is governed from its ten Monasteries of Truth. There the Stone Shamans, above all the Honorbearers, make the weightiest decisions: they name people Truthless and hand out Oathstones, choose the acolytes who will succeed them, and oversee the soldiers' camps beside each monastery. Locally, a Farmer handles the day-to-day running of each area, and Generals command the soldiers.

items.text: Many Shin are pale-skinned.
The Shin tend to have large, round eyes.
Though often called pale, the Shin vary widely in skin tone, and darker shades are common among them.

A Shin name is a given name, then son or daughter, then a parent's name, as in Thresh-son-Esan. To spare a parent dishonour, a grandparent can stand in, as in Szeth-son-son-Vallano. The Heralds are named the same way, as children of God.

The Shin keep apart from other nations and think of them as barbarians, calling them stonewalkers and picturing them like the raiders who sometimes strike their coast. They find the open warfare of the east appalling, believe their own way of setting soldiers apart is better, and feel superior as keepers of the sacred Truth the Heralds gave them: that the Desolations would one day return. Other peoples, in turn, think the Shin barbarians.
Farmers stand highest in Shin society. Farming villages and farmland are held holy, and outsiders may not enter them.

Warriors rank lowest of all, below craftsmen and even merchants, because they exist only to destroy. Anyone who picks up a weapon must take a stone and live out their life as a warrior, obeying whoever holds it in everything. The stone looks ordinary; the obedience is given freely.
The Shin think of a life as adding to the world or subtracting from it. Szeth's shepherding family was meant to add; soldiers, who kill to protect their people, are men who subtract.
The Shin call the darkest part of the night, from the first moon to the second, the "hateful hour": the only time they believe their gods are not watching over them.
Because stone is sacred to the Shin, they will not build with it; their homes are made of clay and earth.

The Shin follow Stone Shamanism. Stone is sacred, the soul passes into stone at death, and mountains have a spirit-soul of their own. Walking on stone or mining it is heresy, and those who do it are scorned as Stonewalkers. Metal is therefore precious, and Soulcast metal is preferred to mined. The Shin also refuse to trade for fabrials, apparently for reasons of faith.
Shin warriors dress in plain brown, so plainly that foreign visitors can take them for servants.
Shin warriors have a script of their own.
Unlike eastern peoples, the Shin do not speak of plants as acting by their own will.
Shin bread was already known in ancient times: in one of Dalinar's visions, Nohadon plans to bake a Shin loaf, fluffier than bread made from other Rosharan grains.
Shin cooks season their food with onions, garlic and other spices, often crushed together in a clay mortar. A favourite dish is misir wat, a thick paste of red lentils.
Those who add seldom eat meat, but those who subtract, such as warriors, eat it often. The Shin also eat many kinds of vegetables, and bread and soda biscuits.

Bargaining with the Shin runs backwards: each side plays down its own goods until they agree, and honesty is rewarded. Most merchants find this baffling, but the Thaylen Vstim is one of the few who understands it, and he does well. The Shin raise chickens, found nowhere else on Roshar, and sell them along with cloth, dried meat and the horses they are famous for.
Within Shinovar, coins are minted from greatshell carapace.
Before humans arrived, Shinovar already had soil but lacked the grass and imported ecology that came with them.
Refugees from Ashyn settled in the sheltered region, bringing plants and animals that could survive away from Roshar's strongest storms.
After the Last Desolation, the Shin took the Honorblades back to Shinovar, and they see themselves as the only ones who remember the truth of Roshar's history.
Early in the Era of Solitude, the Shin tried several times to invade the rest of Roshar with Honorblades, Surges and cavalry, which was very rare elsewhere.
Ishar drew power from the Well of Control and bound himself deeply to Shinovar.
Repeated raids from Steen led the coastal monasteries to develop as defenses against seaborne attacks.

About eight years before the True Desolation, Szeth announced that the Voidbringers were returning. The Shin leaders called it false, made him Truthless and exiled him, trading him to the Thaylen merchant Vstim.
After the first Everstorm, the Shin sent warnings to other countries, including Tashikk.
Dalinar asked them by way of a Thaylen merchant to join his coalition. The Shin declined, sending back only congratulations, and stayed uncommitted.
Szeth completed his struggle against the Honorbearers and the influence controlling Shinovar.
Despite the cleansing, Shinovar was among the lands claimed by Retribution after the contest.

told.title: Refugees from Ashyn
told.text: Humans came to Roshar as refugees from Ashyn and were given this land. The plants and animals they brought took root here, and they still live nowhere else.

told.title: Refugees from Ashyn
told.text: Over seven thousand years ago, humans fled Ashyn, which they had left unfit to live on, and arrived here. The singers gave them this land, which then had soil but no grass. The plants and animals the humans brought took root and came to shape Shinovar's wildlife.

told.title: Spreading out by force
told.text: In time the humans wanted more than the land they had been given, and they took more by violence.

told.title: The kingdom of Shin Kak Nish
told.text: In the age of the Silver Kingdoms, Shinovar was the kingdom of Shin Kak Nish.

told.title: Desolation after Desolation
told.text: Again and again the Desolations threw people back to stone tools. Each time the Heralds returned they helped them rebuild, often as far as the age of bronze, with the Herald Kalak among those who helped.

told.title: War near the border
told.text: Nohadon once told of fighting in a war on the borders of the Shin lands.

when.text: From about 4,500 years before the books

told.title: The Shin take the Honorblades
told.text: After the Last Desolation, the Shin took the Heralds' Honorblades, all but Taln's, home to Shinovar. At some point Nale quietly took his own Blade back without telling their leaders.

After the Last Desolation, the Shin took the Heralds' Honorblades, all but Taln's, home to Shinovar, where their Honorbearers still wield them and their Surges. At some point Nale quietly took his own Blade back without telling their leaders.

told.title: Shin invasions
told.text: Early in the long age after the Last Desolation, the Shin tried more than once to conquer the lands beyond their mountains. Legends tell of great bands of men on horseback, armed with spears.

told.title: Ishar's search for new Heralds
told.text: Ishar worked through the Shin and their Honorblades, seeking people who could replace the Heralds, but no one he found met his standards.

told.title: Ishar binds himself to Shinovar
told.text: About a thousand years ago, Ishar absorbed some of the power of the Well of Control, binding himself deeply to Shinovar. Through the Shin and their Honorblades he sought people who could replace the Heralds, but none satisfied him.

told.title: Ishar's claim about the Unmade
told.text: Ishar told Szeth that when Szeth's father was barely a man, the Shin had accepted Unmade as their gods, and claimed to have saved them from the Unmade.

told.title: Raiders from Steen
told.text: Before the Everstorm, raiders from Steen struck the Shin coast again and again, and the monasteries near the sea grew into strongholds against them.

told.title: A Truthless given away
told.text: Seven years before the books, a Shin farmer gave the Thaylen merchant Vstim a Truthless as a servant. Vstim found him so obedient that he asked for another, but the farmer hopes never to see one like him again.

told.title: Szeth made Truthless
told.text: Szeth warned that the Voidbringers were returning. The Shin leaders declared it false, named him Truthless and banished him with Jezrien's Honorblade, handing him over to the Thaylen merchant Vstim, who often did good business with the Shin.

told.title: The Honorbearers' judgement
told.text: Szeth came to believe that the Voice guiding the Honorbearers was one of the Unmade. He declared that the Desolation had come and led rebels against them. The Honorbearers, his own father among them, judged him and made him Truthless, and the Voice had them let him keep his Honorblade. Szeth gave up his father's name and was sent away east.

told.title: Warnings from the west
told.text: After the Everstorm first struck, the Shin sent warnings to other lands, Tashikk among them, so they could prepare.

told.title: Shinovar stays apart
told.text: Through a Thaylen merchant, Dalinar asked the Shin to join his coalition, keen to win them because they held the westernmost Oathgate on the mainland. They declined, sending back only their congratulations. They never sided with Odium either, and after the Battle of Thaylen Field they remained uncommitted.

told.title: Szeth's quest to cleanse Shinovar
told.text: Szeth came home with Kaladin on a quest to cleanse Shinovar of an Unmade he said had been at work there for years.

told.title: Shinovar cleansed
told.text: What had corrupted Shinovar was Ishar himself, bound to the land. Szeth fought the Honorbearers, his own father last, and struck them down with Nightblood, restoring his homeland.

told.title: Claimed by Retribution
told.text: When Retribution rose, he counted Shinovar among the lands newly under his control, along with the Reshi Isles.
